header.stance: 初領增加、油價回落帶動美債，實質殖利率仍高

zh-TW.long_thesis_markdown:
## 開篇固定收益論點

初領失業救濟金增加、油價大幅回落，帶動6月4日美國公債買盤回流。2年期與5年期殖利率各降3個基點至4.05%與4.18%，10年期及30年期各降2個基點至4.47%與4.97%。前端小幅領漲，曲線略為趨陡，收復部分週三跌幅。

利多主要反映在通膨補償，而非實質利率。10年期損益兩平通膨率下降2個基點，實質殖利率卻維持前一天升高後的水準。初領人數創四個月高點，修正後單位勞動成本漲幅也降低，但生產力較弱，市場仍擔心需求壓力，未放棄聯準會升息的可能；期貨反映年底前升息機率仍接近三分之二。

財政部現金操作順利，焦點開始轉向下週$1,190億附息公債供給。企業仍能融資，條件卻差異很大：Schneider Electric推出股權連結再融資，Reno de Medici債權人則協商取得控制權，Nassau County一家機構還漏付菸草和解債本金。債價回升提供一些喘息，弱現金流與長期資金競爭卻未因此解決。

## 初領人數與油價支持美債反彈

截至5月30日的一週，初領失業救濟金增加1.3萬人至22.5萬人，創四個月最高，超過FactSet預期的21.1萬人，前值則下修至21.2萬人。四週平均由修正後的20萬8,250人增至21萬4,750人。在本週較強的職缺與服務業報告之後，這些數字增加了勞動市場略為降溫的證據。

生產力與勞動成本則好壞參半。第一季非農生產力年化增幅由0.8%下修至0.3%，低於預期的0.7%；單位勞動成本增幅卻也由2.3%降至1.8%。成本壓力減輕，有利通膨補償下降，產出效率變差則使實質利率較難同樣受惠。

油價加強了短期利多。WTI下跌3.10%至$93.04，Brent下跌2.84%至$95.03，回吐前一交易日大部分漲幅。價格仍高，對商品、運輸及肥料成本的影響尚未消退，但當日回落降低了最顯著的近期通膨壓力。

2年期殖利率收於4.05%，5年期4.18%，各降3個基點；10年期及30年期各降2個基點至4.47%及4.97%。2s10s與2s30s利差各擴大1個基點，分別至42與92個基點。相較前一個月累積的趨平，當日只是小幅調整。

10年期損益兩平通膨率下降2個基點至2.36%，實質殖利率維持2.11%。5年期與7年期實質殖利率反而各升2及1個基點至1.70%與1.90%，20年期與30年期各降1個基點至2.50%及2.71%。因此，名目公債雖上漲，中期實質利率的壓力大多仍在。

摩根士丹利Andrew Sheets認為，聯準會較可能將伊朗戰爭視為成長衝擊，而非升息理由，真正的緊縮風險來自核心通膨、財政支持、銀行放款及AI支出。舊金山聯準銀行總裁Mary Daly表示政策位置適當，但官員準備好往任一方向回應。4月PCE年增率3.8%、失業率4.3%之下，初領轉弱仍未消除政策顧慮，年底前升息機率維持約三分之二。

其他市場較平靜，表現卻不一致。S&P 500上漲0.41%，Nasdaq 100下跌0.53%，半導體下跌2.15%；VIX下降4.11%至15.4，美元指數微跌0.12%至99.41，黃金上漲0.88%至$4,475.80。低油價與弱美元有利債券估值，科技股轉弱則與近期多個交易日的強勢形成反差。

## 供給龐大，再融資條件卻大不相同

美國財政部短期標售需求充裕。28天期國庫券接受$750.02億投標，最高得標利率3.615%，投標倍數由2.76升至3.07倍，間接投標者取得51.60%，交易商45.99%。56天期券發行$750.01億，得標利率3.610%，投標倍數由3.08升至3.20倍，間接投標者占65.06%，交易商31.92%。8週券的非交易商參與更強。

國庫券交易也安定。4週附息等值殖利率維持3.68%，6週下降1個基點至3.68%，8週維持3.69%；13週與26週持平於3.71%及3.77%，52週下降2個基點至3.80%。

較大規模的利率風險承接考驗仍在前方。財政部公告$580億新3年券、$390億10年期增額，以及$220億30年期增額，合計$1,190億，與前一個月相同。6、13、26與52週國庫券另合計$2,810億，只有6週規模由$750億降至$650億。

同時，現金管理買回用滿$125億上限，涵蓋一個月至兩年期附息公債。報售金額$416.62億，49檔合格券中買入21檔。買回既有短天期附息債，有助配合國庫券銷售維持流動性，但不減少整體淨舉債需求。

企業也在爭取部分相同的長期買盤。美國投資等級發行達$1兆，速度為2020年以來最快，部分由AI投資帶動。Apollo總裁Jim Zelter表示，今年投資等級發行可能超過美國公債淨銷售，並引述財政年度約$1.4兆新增公債現金融資。這是預測，而非已完成結果，但足以呈現科技、公用事業、國防與政府同時籌資的規模。

Schneider Electric推出€8億2034年到期可轉債，擬議票息0.25%至0.75%，轉換溢價35%至40%。公司計畫用€6.5億買回2030年11月到期可轉債，餘款供一般用途。股價已超過舊券轉換價，再融資可處理股權稀釋風險，同時保留投資人參與資料中心電力及冷卻需求成長的機會。

Reno de Medici需要更根本的調整。Apollo、這家包裝公司與€6億債券持有人達成初步協議，部分債權轉為多數股權，並提供新資金；€1.45億循環額度的放款人仍須納入談判。債券報價約每€1面額26歐分，自由現金流預計到2026年仍負，取得控制權與新增流動性正取代一般再融資。

Nassau County一家機構6月1日漏付$3,600萬本金，成為約$800億菸草和解債市場首宗違約。償付仰賴香菸銷售相關收入，2025年分配給參與州與領地的款項下降19%。2046年券6月2日報58.5美分，未付本金將延後、由未來和解款支應，回收因而取決於持續縮小的現金來源。

Poundstretcher的回收分配則交由法院處理。這家Fortress支持的英國零售商預估7月下旬資金缺口擴大至約£970萬，要求法院批准降租、減免負債，並保留£3,000萬融資額度。按金額計93%的債權人支持，但房東反對；不同意的房東可取得相當於進入破產管理程序時預估回收金額的175%，最低£500。股東資金有助存續，損失如何分攤仍由法院決定。

另一端是尚未投資的承諾資金，正迫使經理人加快部署。收購與私人信貸基金仍持有2020至2022年募集的$6,318億；整體私人資本同期間庫存為$1.28兆，而二至七年前募集的資金達創紀錄$2.5兆。逾40%待投資資金已可運用至少兩年，比例遠高於歷史常態。投資期即將屆滿，可能帶來更多交易與再融資，也可能使急於部署的基金降低授信紀律。

上市信用債基金隨公債上漲，LQD升0.21%、HYG升0.19%、JNK升0.16%。正報酬與現金操作順暢，可以和個別債權損失、重整同時存在，並不代表後者已獲解決。

房貸避險可能放大下一波較大行情。巴克萊估計，票息至少5%的房貸抵押證券已超過$2兆，約三分之一市場接近面額，也是再融資敏感度最高的位置。殖利率上升使預期年限延長，投資人可能賣出美債對沖利率風險；殖利率下降時則反向操作。這未被認定為週四主因，但在公私部門供給考驗市場之際，日益增加的曝險值得關注。

## 各國債市面對不同的通膨與供給

歐元區4月零售量下降0.4%，前月修正後增加0.8%，略弱於預期的下降0.3%。年增率仍有1.0%，但非食品月減0.9%，車用燃油減2.7%。商品需求受限，使央行更難用長期連續緊縮回應能源衝擊。

瑞典5月核心CPIF由零升至0.5%，高於預期中位數0.3%，卻低於央行預測0.9%。整體CPIF由0.8%升至1.5%，接近央行預估，克朗小幅走強。食品與燃油財政減負限制了轉嫁，使1.75%政策利率仍有理由近期維持，即使投資人定價中還有部分緊縮。

捷克5月整體通膨2.1%，低於預期中位數2.3%，符合央行預測。服務通膨降至4.7%，仍高得需要關注。政策利率3.5%之下，數據減弱了立即升息的理由，之後仍須觀察能源是否傳向其他價格。

紐西蘭供給減少有利公債，即使投資人預期央行最終仍會升息。政府下調借款規劃後，NZ$2.25億2031年券獲NZ$14億投標，該券投標倍數創紀錄達6.22倍。預算公布以來，5年期指標殖利率下降逾5個基點。買家因券少、收益有吸引力而進場，無須先改變政策預期。

澳洲已看到高利率對支出的影響。央行今年三次會議都升息，現金利率達4.35%；總裁Michele Bullock以房市轉弱作為早期傳導跡象，4月家庭支出也下降1.1%，跌幅大於預期。前一期提過的第一季GDP僅增0.3%，再添等待理由。不過，Bullock警告，通膨若持續，利率仍須更高、更久，眼前升息無法撤回已發生的油價衝擊。

印度方面，知悉Reliance Industries資金調度討論的人士表示，公司可能轉向較短期貨幣市場工具、減少長債曝險；公司否認對利率或盧比提出正式看法。盧比今年已貶6%，一度接近每$1兌₹97，主權殖利率本季卻大致穩定。在印度央行決策前，這類討論呈現企業如何準備因應匯率防守、進口成本可能引發的政策升息。

## 資金流與債務條件左右新興市場

美元收盤較平靜，亞洲干預卻未結束。韓元跌至2009年以來最低，南韓承諾抑制過度波動；印尼盾創低，印尼也加強干預。印尼與菲律賓先前已升息支持匯率，菲律賓央行另要求銀行確保境外無本金交割衍生工具具有正當經濟目的。印度央行境外美元淨空頭接近$1,000億。這些措施減少失序風險，但也動用準備，或將壓力移到短端利率與本地流動性。

南非則吸引投資組合資金回流。非居民自4月初淨買入ZAR372.9億、約$9.8791億政府債，3月曾創紀錄賣出ZAR561.9億。這段期間10年期殖利率下降67個基點至約8.65%，蘭特兌美元隱含波動率由3月高峰15.9%降至約11%。

央行升息25個基點至7%，加上高實質收益與較低匯率波動，有利這波報酬。蘭特套利交易3月損失4.7%，4月初以來則賺約5%。波動下降與具公信力的本地緊縮恢復了需求，能否延續仍取決於油價、通膨及改革預期。

剛果民主共和國2032年與2037年美元債連漲第三日、維持面額以上，殖利率8.3%與9.03%。雖有伊波拉疫情，主要集中在受衝突影響地區，投資人仍著眼電力、電氣化及AI基礎設施需要的銅與鈷。該國4月首次進入市場籌資$12.5億，高收益與礦產收入支撐債券；若生產或出口受阻，才會更直接威脅主權現金流。

尚比亞下一步取決於價格。摩根士丹利預期，政府可能將提前買回要約由78美分提高至約85美分，2053年券當時報82.14美分。持有逾25%的群體，阻擋了啟動剩餘債券清理所需的約75%接受率。政府想在IMF債務永續條件可能使票息由0.5%升至7.5%之前清償；提高出價可吸引持有人，卻會減少交易節省的成本。

智利增加舉債授權之際，發行也開始付出讓利。2032年披索債定價高於次級市場殖利率12個基點，之後2056年券需要10個基點。政府希望在2026年已允許的$174億之外，再增加$62億。3月總債務占GDP的42.6%，預計2028年超過政府45%的審慎門檻。智利仍有拉丁美洲最高主權評等，但供給增加已將財政偏離計畫轉化為融資成本。

EMB隨美元走軟上漲0.21%。有限的整體漲幅之下，有資金重返南非套利、買家承接剛果礦產曝險、尚比亞要約爭議，以及智利更大的資金需求，各自決定價格。

## 前瞻市場意涵

5月非農就業將於6月5日08:30美東時間公布，接續6月10日08:30 CPI，以及6月11日同時間PPI與初領失業救濟金。非農共識為增加8.5萬人，失業率4.3%。就業逐步降溫、薪資成長受控，將容許目前小幅漲勢延續，但不必然消除升息選項。若勞動組合明顯更弱，之後核心通膨也放慢，較有利實質殖利率下降，尤其2年期與5年期；聘僱強勁或核心及供應鏈漲價擴大，則可能恢復週三壓力。

印度央行6月5日、歐洲央行6月11日決策。若印度維持5.25%政策利率，搭配有效盧比支持，而歐洲央行在任何升息後傳達有限延續空間，將顯示油價回落時各國仍可採取不同回應。原油再漲、進口國匯率走弱或第二輪通膨擴大，都會壓縮這個空間；瑞典與捷克數據則證明，目前轉嫁尚未同步。

美國財政部6月8日至9日國庫券及6月9日至11日附息債標售，將把需求考驗從週四短券延伸出去。$890億13週與$770億26週券6月11日交割，同批另有$650億6週及$500億52週供給；$580億3年、$390億10年與$220億30年附息券6月15日交割。非交易商需求廣、短端殖利率穩定，有利融資維持有序。若非農與CPI之後附息債投標弱，便需要更大供給讓利；企業也在爭取長期買盤之際，房貸避險可能進一步放大調整。

overall_summary.headline: 油價回落、初領人數增加，美國公債收復跌幅
overall_summary.session_narrative:
2年期與5年期美債殖利率各降3個基點至4.05%與4.18%，10年期及30年期各降2個基點至4.47%與4.97%。初領人數升至22.5萬，單位勞動成本修正後增幅降至1.8%，油價也明顯回落。但10年期實質殖利率維持2.11%，名目降幅來自損益兩平通膨率下降2個基點；年底前升息機率仍接近三分之二。

現金操作有序，兩場國庫券標售投標倍數改善，短天期附息債買回用滿$125億。下週附息公債公告合計維持$1,190億，企業借款也加入長期資金競爭。Schneider Electric推出可轉債再融資，Reno de Medici協商債轉股，Nassau County一家機構則漏付菸草和解債本金。

海外支出較弱、通膨不一，使政策仍可分歧，紐西蘭供給減少讓一檔債券獲創紀錄需求。美元雖較平靜，亞洲當局繼續防守匯率。外資重返南非本地債，尚比亞要約價格與智利發行讓利，則讓債務條件成為個別國家表現的關鍵。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Higher jobless claims and a sharp retreat in oil brought buyers back to Treasuries on June 4. The 2- and 5-year yields fell 3 basis points to 4.05% and 4.18%, while the 10-year and 30-year declined 2 to 4.47% and 4.97%. The modest front-end lead produced a small steepening, reversing part of Wednesday's selloff.

The relief was more apparent in inflation compensation than in real rates. Ten-year breakevens fell 2 basis points, with the real yield unchanged at the elevated level reached a day earlier. Claims hit a four-month high and revised unit labor costs rose less than first estimated, but weaker productivity and continued concern over underlying demand kept markets from dismissing a Fed increase. Futures still put the year-end probability near two-thirds.

Treasury's cash operations went smoothly as attention turned to next week's $119 billion coupon calendar. Corporate funding remained available too, though the terms varied sharply: Schneider Electric launched an equity-linked refinancing, while Reno de Medici creditors negotiated control and a Nassau County agency missed principal on tobacco-settlement debt. A recovery in bond prices was giving borrowers some relief, without resolving weak cash flows or the competition for long-term capital.

## Claims and Oil Give Treasuries a Lift

Initial claims rose 13,000 to 225,000 in the week ended May 30, their highest in four months. The figure exceeded the 211,000 FactSet consensus and followed a downwardly revised 212,000. The four-week average increased to 214,750 from a revised 208,250, adding evidence of some labor-market cooling after the stronger openings and services reports earlier in the week.

Productivity and labor costs gave a mixed signal. Q1 nonfarm productivity growth was revised to an annualized 0.3% from 0.8%, below a 0.7% forecast. Unit labor-cost growth was nevertheless revised down to 1.8% from 2.3%. Less cost pressure helped inflation compensation ease, while poorer output efficiency offered less reassurance about the real-rate outlook.

Oil reinforced the immediate relief. WTI fell 3.10% to $93.04 and Brent declined 2.84% to $95.03, reversing much of the previous session's increase. Prices remained high enough to affect goods, transport and fertilizer, but the daily retreat reduced the most visible source of near-term inflation pressure.

The 2-year yield closed at 4.05% and the 5-year at 4.18%, each down 3 basis points; the 10-year and 30-year fell 2 to 4.47% and 4.97%. The 2s10s and 2s30s curves each steepened 1 basis point, to 42 and 92. It was a small adjustment against the larger flattening of the preceding month.

At 10 years, the breakeven dropped 2 basis points to 2.36%, while the real yield stayed at 2.11%. Five- and seven-year real yields rose 2 and 1 basis points to 1.70% and 1.90%; 20- and 30-year real yields each fell 1 to 2.50% and 2.71%. The nominal rally therefore left much of the real-rate pressure in intermediate maturities intact.

Morgan Stanley's Andrew Sheets argued that the Fed was more likely to regard the Iran war as a growth shock than as the reason for an increase. He located the tightening risk instead in core inflation, fiscal support, bank lending and AI spending. San Francisco Fed President Mary Daly said policy was well placed but officials were ready to act in either direction. With annual PCE inflation at 3.8% in April and unemployment at 4.3%, the softer claims report did not eliminate the policy concern behind the roughly two-thirds year-end hike probability.

Markets beyond rates showed a calmer but uneven session. The S&P 500 rose 0.41%, while the Nasdaq 100 fell 0.53% and semiconductors declined 2.15%. The VIX dropped 4.11% to 15.4, and the dollar index slipped 0.12% to 99.41. Gold gained 0.88% to $4,475.80. Lower oil and a softer dollar helped bond valuations, while the technology retreat contrasted with the strength that had accompanied several recent sessions.

## Heavy Supply Meets Very Different Refinancing Terms

Treasury's short-term auctions attracted ample demand. It accepted $75.002 billion of 28-day bills at a 3.615% high rate and 3.07 bid-to-cover, up from 2.76. Indirect bidders received 51.60% and dealers 45.99%. The $75.001 billion 56-day sale cleared at 3.610% with 3.20 cover, compared with 3.08 previously; indirect bidders took 65.06% and dealers 31.92%. The eight-week sale had the stronger nondealer participation.

Bill trading was similarly quiet. Four-week coupon-equivalent yields held at 3.68%, six-week yields fell 1 basis point to 3.68%, and eight-week yields stayed at 3.69%. Thirteen- and 26-week yields were unchanged at 3.71% and 3.77%, while the 52-week fell 2 basis points to 3.80%.

The larger duration test is still ahead. Treasury announced $58 billion of new 3-year notes, a $39 billion 10-year reopening and a $22 billion 30-year reopening, totaling $119 billion and unchanged from the prior monthly cycle. Another $281 billion was announced across six-, 13-, 26- and 52-week bills. Only the six-week size was reduced, to $65 billion from $75 billion.

At the same time, a cash-management buyback accepted the full $12.5 billion cap in one-month to two-year coupons. Treasury received $41.662 billion of offers and bought 21 of 49 eligible issues. Removing seasoned short coupons helped liquidity alongside the bill sales, without reducing the broader net borrowing requirement.

Corporate issuance is competing for some of the same long-term demand. US investment-grade sales reached $1 trillion at the fastest pace since 2020, partly driven by AI investment. Apollo President Jim Zelter said annual investment-grade issuance could exceed net Treasury sales, citing about $1.4 trillion of new Treasury cash financing in the fiscal year. That is a forecast rather than a completed comparison, but points to the scale of technology, utilities, defense and government borrowing seeking investors.

Schneider Electric launched an €800 million convertible due in 2034, with a proposed coupon of 0.25%-0.75% and a conversion premium of 35%-40%. It planned to spend €650 million repurchasing a convertible due in November 2030, with the balance for general purposes. Its shares had risen above the old bond's conversion price. Refinancing would address dilution risk while preserving investors' exposure to data-center power and cooling demand.

Reno de Medici needed a more fundamental change. Apollo, the packaging company and holders of its €600 million bonds reached a preliminary agreement to convert part of the claims into majority equity and provide new funding. Lenders on a €145 million revolving facility still had to be included in negotiations. With bonds near 26 cents on the euro and free cash flow expected to remain negative through 2026, ownership and new liquidity were replacing ordinary refinancing.

A Nassau County agency missed $36 million of principal on June 1, the first default in the roughly $80 billion tobacco-settlement bond sector. Payments depend on cigarette sales, and distributions to participating states and territories fell 19% in 2025. The 2046 bonds traded at 58.5 cents on June 2. Unpaid principal is extended against future settlement revenue, leaving recovery dependent on a shrinking source of cash.

Poundstretcher's recovery allocation was headed to court. The Fortress-backed UK retailer sought approval to lower rents, write off liabilities and retain a £30 million funding facility as its projected shortfall widened toward £9.7 million by late July. Creditors representing 93% by value supported the plan, but landlords objected. Dissenting landlords were offered 175% of estimated administration recovery, with a £500 minimum. Sponsor funding improved the prospect of survival; the court would decide how the losses were shared.

At the other end of the market, aging unspent commitments were pressing managers to invest. Buyout and private-credit funds still held $631.8 billion raised during 2020-22. Across private capital, the comparable stockpile was $1.28 trillion, and money raised two to seven years earlier reached a record $2.5 trillion. More than 40% of dry powder had been available for at least two years, well above its historical share. Investment-period deadlines could bring more deals and refinancing, with a risk that urgency weakens underwriting discipline.

Listed credit funds gained with Treasuries: LQD rose 0.21%, HYG 0.19% and JNK 0.16%. The positive returns and smooth cash operations coexisted with the creditor losses and restructurings rather than resolving them.

Mortgage hedging could amplify the next larger rate move. Barclays said more than $2 trillion of mortgage securities carried coupons of at least 5%, with roughly one-third of the market near par, where refinancing sensitivity is greatest. Rising yields extend expected lives and can prompt Treasury sales to hedge duration; falling yields can reverse the flow. This was not identified as Thursday's main driver, but the growing exposure matters as public and corporate supply tests the market.

## National Bond Markets Follow Different Inflation and Supply Paths

Euro-area retail volumes fell 0.4% in April after a revised 0.8% March gain, slightly weaker than the expected 0.3% decline. Sales were 1.0% higher than a year earlier, but non-food volumes dropped 0.9% on the month and automotive fuel fell 2.7%. Restrained goods demand complicated the case for a prolonged tightening response to the energy shock.

Swedish core CPIF inflation rose to 0.5% in May from zero, above the 0.3% survey median but below the Riksbank's 0.9% projection. Headline CPIF increased to 1.5% from 0.8%, close to the central bank's forecast, and the krona strengthened modestly. Fiscal relief on food and fuel had limited pass-through, supporting the 1.75% policy rate as a near-term anchor despite some tightening priced by investors.

Czech headline inflation was 2.1% in May, below a 2.3% median estimate and in line with the central bank's projection. Services inflation slowed to 4.7%, still high enough to warrant attention. With the policy rate at 3.5%, the numbers weakened the immediate case for an increase, leaving later decisions sensitive to energy passing into underlying prices.

Scarcer supply supported New Zealand government debt even as investors expected eventual Reserve Bank tightening. A NZ$225 million sale of 2031 bonds drew NZ$1.4 billion of bids, a record 6.22 cover for the security, after the government reduced projected borrowing. The benchmark 5-year yield had fallen more than 5 basis points since the budget. Buyers were responding to fewer bonds and attractive carry without needing a different policy outlook.

Australia was already seeing the effect of higher rates on spending. The RBA had increased the cash rate at all three meetings that year to 4.35%. Governor Michele Bullock cited softer housing as an early sign of transmission, while April household spending fell a larger-than-expected 1.1%. The weak 0.3% Q1 GDP reading reported previously added to the argument for patience. Bullock nevertheless warned that persistent inflation would require higher rates for longer; current increases could not undo the oil-price shock already under way.

In India, people familiar with Reliance Industries' treasury discussions described possible moves into shorter money-market paper and reduced long-bond exposure. The company denied expressing a formal view on rates or the rupee. The currency was down 6% during the year and had approached 97 per dollar, even though sovereign yields were broadly stable during the quarter. The discussions, ahead of the RBI decision, reflected how companies might manage duration if currency defense and imported costs led to higher policy rates.

## Flows and Debt Terms Drive Emerging-Market Pricing

The quieter dollar close did not end Asian currency intervention. South Korea pledged to curb excessive volatility as the won reached its weakest since 2009, and Indonesia intensified intervention as the rupiah hit a record low. Indonesia and the Philippines had already raised policy rates to support their currencies. The Philippine central bank also told banks to ensure offshore nondeliverable derivatives served legitimate economic purposes. The RBI's net short-dollar offshore position was close to $100 billion. Those responses helped contain disorder while using reserves or shifting pressure into short rates and local liquidity.

South Africa was drawing portfolio money back. Nonresidents bought a net 37.29 billion rand, about $987.91 million, of government bonds from early April after a record 56.19 billion rand selloff in March. The 10-year yield fell 67 basis points to about 8.65% over the period. Rand-dollar implied volatility declined to roughly 11% from a March peak of 15.9%.

The Reserve Bank's 25-basis-point increase to 7%, high real carry and lower currency volatility helped the return. The rand carry trade gained about 5% from early April after losing 4.7% in March. Lower volatility and credible domestic tightening had restored demand, with oil, inflation and reform expectations still important to whether it would last.

The Democratic Republic of Congo's 2032 and 2037 dollar bonds rose for a third session and stayed above par, yielding 8.3% and 9.03%. Investors focused on copper and cobalt demand from power, electrification and AI infrastructure despite an Ebola outbreak concentrated in a conflict-affected region. Congo had raised $1.25 billion in its April market debut. High carry and mineral revenue supported the bonds; disruption to production or exports would be the more direct threat to sovereign cash flow.

Zambia's next step depended on the price offered. Morgan Stanley expected the government might raise its early buyback offer to about 85 cents from 78, while the 2053 bond traded at 82.14 cents. A group holding more than 25% was blocking the roughly 75% acceptance needed for a cleanup call. The government sought to retire the debt before a possible coupon increase from 0.5% to 7.5% under IMF debt-sustainability conditions. Paying more could attract holders while reducing the savings from the transaction.

Chile's additional borrowing request was now accompanied by issuance concessions. Its 2032 peso bonds cleared 12 basis points above secondary-market yields, and a later 2056 sale required 10 basis points. The government wanted another $6.2 billion of authorization beyond the $17.4 billion already permitted for 2026. Gross debt stood at 42.6% of GDP in March and was projected to exceed the 45% prudence threshold by 2028. Chile retained Latin America's highest sovereign ratings, but the growing supply was translating fiscal slippage into borrowing costs.

EMB rose 0.21% with the softer dollar. The modest aggregate gain covered very different positions: investors returning to South African carry, buyers taking Congo's commodity exposure, Zambia's contested tender and Chile's larger funding requirements.

## Forward Market Significance

May payrolls are due June 5 at 08:30 ET, followed by CPI June 10 at 08:30 ET and PPI and weekly claims June 11 at the same time. The payroll consensus is 85,000, with unemployment expected at 4.3%. A gradual cooling in employment and contained wage growth would leave room for the current modest rally, without necessarily removing the Fed's tightening option. A much weaker labor mix followed by softer core inflation would favor lower real yields, especially in the 2- and 5-year sectors. Strong hiring or broader core and pipeline price increases would instead revive Wednesday's pressure.

The RBI decides June 5 and the ECB June 11. An unchanged 5.25% Indian policy rate with effective rupee support, alongside limited follow-through signaled by the ECB after any increase, would show room for different national responses as oil retreats. Renewed crude gains, weaker importer currencies or wider second-round inflation would narrow that room. The Swedish and Czech figures provide evidence that pass-through has not been uniform.

Treasury's June 8-9 bill auctions and June 9-11 coupon sequence will extend the demand test beyond Thursday's short-term sales. The $89 billion 13-week and $77 billion 26-week bills settle June 11, alongside $65 billion of six-week and $50 billion of 52-week supply. The $58 billion 3-year, $39 billion 10-year and $22 billion 30-year coupons settle June 15. Broad nondealer demand and stable short yields would support continued orderly financing. Weak coupon bidding after payrolls and CPI would require more supply concession, with mortgage hedging potentially amplifying the adjustment as corporate borrowers compete for duration buyers.
